  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  INTRODUCTION TO COMMNUNICATION SYSTEMS [ECE_4313]  
  Marks: 50                                                                                  Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)            Apply the Nyquist Sampling Theorem to explain how it is used in converting an analog  
  audio signal into its digital form, and demonstrate its significance in real-world audio  
  (5)  
  recording systems.  
  A)  
  B)       Explain how data rate is influenced by available bandwidth.                                 (3)  
  C)       Illustrate the relationship between modulation technique and required bandwidth             (2)  
  2)            Illustrate the structure and working principle of an optical fibre, and analyze its  
  advantages over conventional transmission media.  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)       Apply the concept of Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) to explain how  
  multiple signals can be transmitted simultaneously through a single fibre.                  (3)  
  
  C)       Interpret one major benefit and one challenge of optical communication in modern  
  networks.                                                                                   (2)  
  
  3)            Differentiate between direct broadcast satellite and digital satellite radio in terms of  
  coverage and usage.  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)       Apply how data analytics differs from cloud computing in function and purpose.              (3)  
  C)       Interpret the unique advantage of ultrawideband (UWB) compared to other wireless  
  communication technologies.                                                                 (2)  
  
  4)            Explain the concept of frequency reuse in cellular communication. Apply it to show how  
  it helps improve spectrum efficiency in a dense urban network.  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)       Compare macro cells and micro cells by applying them to rural vs. city environments.        (3)  
  C)       Demonstrate how cell splitting improves capacity in a dense urban area.                     (2)
